column1: # Surface the coverage gate may not demand a check for, and why.
# One entry per line: the action name or the accessibility identifier, a TAB,
# and the reason no check can reach it.
# **An entry is a redirect, never an exemption.** It is printed on every run of
# `make e2e`, exactly as a quarantined check and a backfilled one are, because
# a list nobody is reminded of is a list that grows. A reviewer reads the
# reason; nothing here judges whether it is a good one, because nothing here
# **The bar is "no check can reach it", not "no check reaches it yet".** The
# second is ordinary work and the gate is asking for it. The first is a claim
# about the harness — a control that only exists while a menu is open, an
# action whose only effect is to end the run that would assert it — and it
# should be rare enough that a line here is worth arguing about.
# **Three kinds of entry live below, and the second is the one that does not
# meet the bar properly.** It is a redirect to a named ticket, kept here
# because the gate has to say something and a silent gap says nothing. It is
# the one to argue with first.
#   2. blocked on #254 — the browser leg has no seeded login binary
#   3. drawn only over a reply, and no fixture host ever replies
#   4. not a control — drawn text the checks READ, which no act can press
#   5. a control drawn only while a write is in flight, which the fixture never prolongs
# A `parity` step drives one action down both channels with the SAME params and
# compares the state each left. That shape cannot describe a destructive or
# creative action: the click consumes its own subject, so the dispatch that
# follows is either refused (the id is gone) or acts on something else (a new
# id). Covering these needs a parity step that can carry different params per
# channel, or compare the shape of a change rather than the state after it —
# harness work with its own argument to make, and out of 2e's scope.

column2: its parity: the click removes the binding, so the dispatch half cannot be given the same id. Dispatch and both channels' behaviour ARE covered by 2e-settings-unlink.jsonl; what no check can express is the comparison.
its parity: the click creates a binding under an id, so a dispatch with the same params collides with what the click just made. Covered by 2e-settings-doors.jsonl up to the browser leg.

its parity: the click returns the binding to its hole, and api_unbind refuses a position that holds no binding (`unbindNotABinding`), so the dispatch half cannot be given the same params — and a re-drag between the halves is not expressible. Both channels ARE covered by api-unbind.jsonl, each after its own drag, asserting the same hole back through read_pane; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity: the click cancels the send in flight, and api_cancel refuses a pane with nothing in flight (`nothingInFlight`), so the dispatch half cannot be given the same state — and a second Send between the halves is not expressible. Both channels ARE covered by api-cancel.jsonl, each after its own Send, asserting the same cancelled response through read_pane; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity: the click (or Esc) cancels the read in flight, and db_cancel refuses a pane with nothing running (`nothing is running on pane …`), so the dispatch half cannot be given the same state — and a second slow read between the halves is not expressible inside one parity step, api_cancel's case. Both channels ARE covered: db-cancel-click.jsonl cancels one recursive-CTE read by db.<pane>.cancel and the next by dispatch, asserting the same state after each through read_pane (running false, cancelledAfterMs, the previous 2 rows kept, sort empty) and "cancelled after" in the tree; db-cancel-escape.jsonl cancels by Esc. What no check can express is the comparison.

its parity: the UI half of a parity step is a click or a drag, and the operator's channel is a paste (cmd+v into the path editor), so the comparison cannot be expressed. Both channels ARE covered: the dispatch by api-paste-curl.jsonl, the paste by api-paste-curl-hotkey.jsonl, each asserting the same draft and the Filled from cURL line; what no check can express is the comparison.

display text, not a control: a static `Text` (DBPane.swift) carrying Format's refusal reason, with no press action, and the vocabulary addresses only `click`/`focus` by identifier while `expect.tree` matches by text, so no step can "press" it. Its content IS asserted: db-query-line-not-formatted.jsonl expects `not formatted: a string opened at character 39 never closes` in the tree, then its absence after the next edit.

its parity (3a-i): the operator's channel is ↑↓ with the diff open — keys, not a click or a drag — so the UI half of a parity step cannot be expressed, on api_fill_from_curl's precedent. The dispatch is covered by 3a-i-git-drill.jsonl (across roots, both directions, asserting the selection and the header through read_pane and the tree). The keyboard half is 3a-i-git-keys.jsonl: ↑↓ folded, across both roots, asserting the selection through read_pane.

its parity (3a-i): the operator's channel is Esc — a key, not a click or a drag — so the UI half of a parity step cannot be expressed. The dispatch is covered by 3a-i-git-drill.jsonl (unfold keeps the selection, the list is back). The keyboard half is 3a-i-git-keys.jsonl: Esc unfolds with the same file selected.

its parity (3a-i): there is no operator control for it at all — GitPane folds only by selecting, so git_fold is the agent's alone and no UI half exists to compare. The dispatch is covered by 3a-i-git-drill.jsonl (fold again, the same file and position).

its parity: the operator's channel is the agent's own stream — the window records a `rate_limit_event` frame from a turn on its own, with no click or drag — so the UI half of a parity step cannot be expressed, on git_fold's precedent. Both channels ARE covered: the dispatch by capacity-low-reading.jsonl and capacity-passed-reset.jsonl, the stream by agent/capacity-after-turn.jsonl, each asserting the reading it lands on the indicator; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity: the Undo click forgets the fill it undoes, and api_undo_fill refuses a pane with nothing to undo, so the dispatch half cannot be given the same state after the click — and a second fill between the halves is not expressible inside one parity step. Both channels ARE covered by api-paste-curl.jsonl, the click after one fill and the dispatch after another, each asserting the same restored draft through read_pane; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity: the click removes the database, and removing one that is gone is refused (`no database … in environment …`), so the dispatch half cannot be given the same params. Dispatch is covered by 2e-settings-databases-dispatch.jsonl and the click by 2e-settings-databases.jsonl; what no check can express is the comparison.

its parity: the only UI path is the `Settings…` MENU item, and a menu's buttons are not in the accessibility tree until the menu is open — the same rule that excuses every other menu control. Checks drive it by its real gesture, cmd+comma, and 2e-settings-pane.jsonl also dispatches it.

its dispatch: it needs a row id, which is minted per send and published only in read_pane — the same reason api_render_curl below is here. The operator's gesture IS covered: api-recent.jsonl presses api.recent.0.reopen and asserts the draft it rebuilds. Permanent, not blocked: nothing in the vocabulary carries a value from read_pane into a dispatch.

Two reasons, and the second is the one that lasts. A dispatch cannot hold the row id, which is minted per send and published only in read_pane; and the operator's own Copy as cURL puts its line on the PASTEBOARD, which no check can read — the act is real and its result leaves the window. `api_reopen`'s CLICK left this file when the recent strip gave it a button, because a reopen's effect lands in the draft where a check can see it; its dispatch half is still here, for the first of these reasons. Covered by WakilKitTests: curlIsPastTenseOnly, curlOnlyMentionsACredentialThereWasOne, curlEmitsAndNeverParses.

Its whole effect is a string on the SYSTEM PASTEBOARD, which no check can read — the act is real and its result leaves the window, so a check could press it and assert nothing, which is the check-that-cannot-fail this file exists to prevent rather than permit. `TerminalPane`'s own Copy is silent for the same reason and carries no indicator. The line it copies is `apiRenderCurl`'s, covered by WakilKitTests: curlIsPastTenseOnly, curlOnlyMentionsACredentialThereWasOne, curlEmitsAndNeverParses. If this pane ever draws a "copied" acknowledgement, the act becomes observable and this line should go.

its parity (3b-i): the operator's channel is ⌘T, a menu key equivalent — a key, not a click or a drag — on git_step's precedent; the empty pane only names the key. The dispatch is covered by most 3b-i-editor-* checks; ⌘T by 3b-i-editor-scratch-save.jsonl and 3b-i-editor-close-keys.jsonl, asserting the Untitled-N tab through read_pane.

its parity (3b-i): the operator's channels are ⌘W (a key) and the unsaved prompt's Don't Save, and the click consumes its own subject — the dispatch half after it would close a different tab or be refused (`the editor pane has no open tab`), api_cancel's case. Both channels ARE covered: 3b-i-editor-close-keys.jsonl (⌘W clean, ⌘W dirty → Esc / Cancel / Don't Save) and the dispatch with and without discard in 3b-i-editor-refusals.jsonl.

its parity (3b-i): there is no operator control for it — the operator moves the cursor inside Monaco, the one non-action path (design-language §11), so no UI half exists to compare, on git_fold's precedent. The dispatch is covered by 3b-i-editor-tabs-language.jsonl (cursor.line and cursor.column through read_pane) and refused on an empty pane in 3b-i-editor-refusals.jsonl.

its parity (3b-i): no operator control — the operator selects inside Monaco, the one non-action path, so no UI half exists. The dispatch is covered by most 3b-i-editor-* checks, which read selected_text back to prove what a save wrote.

its parity (3b-i): no operator control — the operator's own edits are typing in Monaco, the one non-action path (`editorBufferDidChange`), so no UI half exists. The dispatch is covered by most 3b-i-editor-* checks, and its read-only refusal by 3b-i-editor-read-only.jsonl.

its parity (3b-i): no operator control — it runs when a window relaunches onto saved tabs, and one check is one launch. The dispatch is covered by 3b-i-editor-disk-changed.jsonl (an open, dirty tab is kept as it is); restoring after a relaunch is the runbook's row 9.

its parity (3b-ii-b): the click replaces, and the same dispatch after it finds nothing left to replace and answers a different last_replace, so the two halves cannot read back the same pane (api_cancel's case: the click consumes its own subject). Both channels ARE covered: the click (Replace All) by 3b-ii-b-replace-all.jsonl and the dispatch by 3b-ii-b-replace-undo.jsonl, each asserting last_replace's files and the Replaced … line; Replace in this file by 3b-ii-b-replace-file.jsonl, and Cancel by 3b-ii-b-replace-cancel.jsonl.

its parity (3b-ii-b): the Undo click spends the pane's one undo, and the dispatch after it is then refused (`no replace to undo`) — api_undo_fill's case. The click is 3b-ii-b-replace-undo.jsonl's (undone, restored 2, and the changed-since line for the file changed on disk), and so is the refusal of the dispatch after it.

its parity (3b-ii-b): the drag moves a tab, and the same {from, to} dispatched on the moved strip moves a different tab, so the two halves cannot read back the same order. The drag and the dispatch are each 3b-ii-b-tab-move.jsonl's, each asserting the strip's order and the active tab through read_pane.

column1: # Every one of these needs a real browser trip and a real one-year credential at
# Anthropic. A check that reached them would mint a credential on every run,
# which is a side effect no gate is worth. #254 is the ticket for a seeded login
# binary on the provider record; these become ordinary work the day it lands.
# #254 was PARKED on 2026-09-26 (docs/wakil/parked.md), not done — closed with
# the tracker's move to a bug inbox — so every line below still stands. #325
# (Adopt and Register vanish under a sign-in error banner) is walk-only for the
# same reason: the banner is drawn only by a trip that started, and the one
# made-up claude path that fails safely today would be a real browser trip if

column2: #254. Opens a browser on the operator's machine and authenticates as them. No harness can drive it and none should: every run would leave a real credential behind.
#254. The control that does the above.
#254. Goes straight to the browser by design — no confirmation step — so pressing it IS starting a real trip.
#254. Starts a fresh trip, and only appears when the config dir is already signed in, which itself needs a real credential.
#254. Only exists while a browser trip is in flight.
#254. Only exists while waiting on a live mint.
#254. Drawn only by the states a finished trip reaches — added, refused, cancelled, timedOut, uncertain, failed.

column1: # The fixture's entries resolve to `.invalid` hosts on purpose, and the one live
# listener (`slow`) never answers; wakil-http refuses a cleartext origin, so no
# fixture server can answer either. A control drawn only over a reply cannot be
# reached by any check. The runbook's check 5 walks it against a real API.

column2: the Body · Headers choice (W20) is drawn only over a reply, and no fixture host ever replies — every entry is `.invalid` or the never-answering `slow`, and wakil-http refuses http://. apiResponseOffersHeaders and apiResponseHeaderRows are pinned in ApiPaneLayoutTests; the drawn table is the runbook's check 5.

column1: # ---- 4. Not a control: drawn text the checks read ----------------------------
# 2d-ii put identifiers on views that draw text and take no input. The gate
# counts an identifier covered only when a check clicks, focuses, types into or
# drags it, and none of those acts applies to a static text or a container: an
# AXPress on one is refused (action unsupported) and AXFocused is not settable.
# What each says IS asserted, through `expect.tree`, in the checks named — the
# vocabulary just has no way to credit a read to an identifier. If a read ever
# counts as coverage, every line here should go.

column2: the composer bar's container (.contain), which holds the field, the heard text and the hint and takes no input itself. Its contents are read by every 2d-ii voice check; the field inside it is `window.composer`, which they type into.

a Text: the words heard while ⌥ is held, or the notice that replaces them. Read, not pressed — 2d-ii-voice-silence.jsonl asserts "Hearing nothing from E2E Microphone" and the words that clear it; 2d-ii-voice-lands-unsent.jsonl and 2d-ii-voice-escape.jsonl assert the words mid-hold.

a Text: the bar's hint. Read, not pressed — the keys hint ("TO SPEAK"), the listening hint ("RELEASE TO PUT IT IN THE LINE") and the landed hint ("HEARD · RETURN SENDS · EDIT FIRST") are asserted by the 2d-ii voice checks.

the thought thread's container (.contain), which takes hits only on its rows and the "earlier" line. Its rows are pressed by 2d-ii-thread-earlier.jsonl as window.thread.row.<id> and window.thread.earlier.

a Text: the Speech row's "unknown engine 'x', using Apple". Read, not pressed — 2d-ii-settings-speech.jsonl asserts it after a dispatched unknown id and a reload, and its absence after Apple is chosen.

the git pane's container (3a-i): it holds the list or the spine and diff, has no press action, and refuses AXFocused (measured: axresolve not_focusable) — its keyboard focus is SwiftUI's own, given when the pane is focused. What it draws is read by every 3a-i check; its rows are `git.row:…`.

a Text (3a-i): a root's header, `e2e-api · main` or `e2e-git · not a git repository`. Read, not pressed — 3a-i-git-list.jsonl asserts both, and 3a-i-git-live.jsonl asserts `e2e-portal · main · clean` once the root empties.

a Text (3a-i): the second and later lines of a root's error, drawn whole beneath its header — and only when the error HAS a second line. The fixture's non-repository error is one line, so it is never drawn; its split is pinned by WakilKitTests aLongErrorIsSplitBetweenTheHeaderAndTheLinesBeneath, and a multi-line error is the runbook's walk.
a Text (3a-i): `root / path · n of N · ↑↓`. Read, not pressed — 3a-i-git-drill.jsonl asserts it at 1, 2, 4 and 5 of 5, across both roots.

a Text (3a-i): `binary · 2.1 MB` or `file is 3.0 MB · first 2 MB shown`, drawn only over a binary or oversized diff. Display text with no press action; its wording is pinned by WakilKitTests banners and smallBinarySizes, and wakil-git's caps by its Go tests.
a Text (3a-i): a diff's error, drawn whole. Display text with no press action; the fixture's diffs all load, and `diff.error` is asserted null by 3a-i-git-drill.jsonl.

the Monaco host's container (3a-i): an NSViewRepresentable holding the WKWebView, with no press action of its own. 3a-i-git-drill.jsonl asserts the web view is mounted (`HTML content` in the tree); what it shows is the operator's ruling (§5 tones), not a check's.

the load tick (3a-i, Rule 5): a 2 pt shape drawn only while a read or a diff is in flight, which against the fixture's tiny repositories lasts a few milliseconds — never long enough for a tree read to see. Pinned by WakilKitTests theClickedRowCarriesTheLoadingMarkUntilItsDiffArrives; seeing it is the runbook's walk.

the palette's container (.contain, palette rework): it holds the header, the query line, the rows and the footer, and takes no input itself — the dimmer around it takes the dismissing click. Its contents are read by every palette-*.jsonl check ("OPEN OR SWITCH TO", "RUN A COMMAND", the "N of M" count); the field inside it is palette.query, typed into, and its rows are palette.row.<id>, pressed.

a Text (palette rework): an input step's title, uppercased, where the mode's name was. Read, not pressed — palette-command-step.jsonl and palette-escape.jsonl assert "PANE KIND", palette-run-error.jsonl "CURL COMMAND", palette-switch-environment.jsonl "ENVIRONMENT", palette-table-row.jsonl a drill's "BOOKINGS"; palette-escape.jsonl asserts it gone after one Esc.

a Text (palette rework, rule 8): a run's error, drawn whole under the query line. Display text with no press action. Read, not pressed — palette-run-error.jsonl asserts "no entry in staging has that host" with the step and the typed line still there.

the Settings capacity strip's scroll container (provider capacity), which takes no input. Its rows are read by capacity-low-reading.jsonl and capacity-passed-reset.jsonl, beside the accounts table's own CREDENTIAL and SIGN-IN headers.

the capacity indicator beside ACCOUNT (provider capacity): it has no press action, and it refuses AXFocused (measured 2026-10-10: axresolve not_focusable), because `.focusable(interactions: .activate)` keeps a click from taking the composer's focus (Rule 6) and joins the key loop only with macOS Keyboard navigation on. Its card opens on hover or on that focus, and the vocabulary has no hover step, so opening the card is walk-only. What it draws is read by capacity-at-launch.jsonl (the launch probe, no turn), capacity-low-reading.jsonl, capacity-passed-reset.jsonl and agent/capacity-after-turn.jsonl.

the Monaco host's container (3b-i): an NSViewRepresentable holding the WKWebView, with no press action of its own (git.diff's case). Typing into it is driven by keys: 3b-i-editor-scratch-save.jsonl types after ⌘T and after a save, and asserts the text through read_pane.
a Text (3b-i, Rule 8): a tab's notice, drawn whole. Read, not pressed — 3b-i-editor-read-only.jsonl asserts "ro.bin is a binary file" in the tree and through read_pane.

the disk line's container (.contain, 3b-i): its text and two buttons. Read, not pressed — 3b-i-editor-disk-changed.jsonl asserts "disk.txt changed on disk" and its absence while comparing and after Reload; its buttons are editor.reload and editor.compare, pressed.

Compare's Monaco host (3b-i): a WKWebView container with no press action. 3b-i-editor-disk-changed.jsonl asserts Compare's header opens and closes (button and Esc); what the diff shows is the operator's ruling (runbook row 6).

a Text (3b-i, Rule 8): drawn only when the file cannot be read back for Compare. The fixture's files are always readable and no step can make one unreadable mid-launch; display text with no press action either way. The runbook walks Compare.

a Text (3b-i, Rule 8): the path field's failure, drawn whole. Read, not pressed — 3b-i-editor-save-as-field.jsonl asserts "is outside the active project's roots; editor reads and writes are confined to them (Invariant 6, Decision 36)" with the typed path still in the field.

the empty pane's hint (3b-i, .combine): "⌘P to open a file · ⌘T for a scratch tab", with no press action. Read, not pressed — 3b-i-editor-close-keys.jsonl asserts it after the last tab closes, and its absence after ⌘W closes the pane.

the unsaved prompt's container (.contain, 3b-i): the message and three buttons. Read, not pressed — every prompt check asserts its message; its buttons editor.unsaved.save / .dontSave / .cancel are pressed by 3b-i-editor-close-keys.jsonl, 3b-i-editor-unsaved-save.jsonl and 3b-i-editor-unsaved-org-switch.jsonl.

a Text (3b-i): the prompt's question. Read, not pressed — "Save changes to Untitled-2?" (3b-i-editor-close-keys.jsonl), "Save changes to kept.txt?" (3b-i-editor-unsaved-save.jsonl), "Unsaved changes in Untitled-1" (3b-i-editor-unsaved-org-switch.jsonl, 3b-i-editor-unsaved-quit.jsonl).

the saving tick (3b-i, Rule 5): a 2 pt shape drawn only while a write is in flight, which against the fixture's tiny files lasts milliseconds — never long enough for a tree read to see (git.loading's case). `saving` is asserted false after each save through read_pane; seeing the tick is the runbook's walk.

the row detail strip's container (.contain, RowDetailStrip.swift): its labels and values, with no press action of its own. What it draws is read by db-detail-strip.jsonl and db-detail-big-cells.jsonl; its values are db.<pane>.detail.<i>, read.

a Text (db pane footer): the flight line, "running …" while a read is in flight and "cancelled after …" once one is cancelled. Read, not pressed — db-cancel-click.jsonl and db-cancel-escape.jsonl assert "cancelled after" in the tree, and db-cancel-click.jsonl its absence after the next read.

the db grid's surface (.contain): it has no press action and refuses AXFocused (measured: axresolve not_focusable), git.pane's case — its keyboard focus is SwiftUI's own, given when the pane is focused, which the checks do by clicking rail.db-<n>. Its keys are driven that way: ↑↓, Space and Esc by db-detail-strip.jsonl, ⌘C by db-grid-copy.jsonl; its rows' contents are read through read_pane.

the row's ⓘ: drawn only while the pointer hovers inside a row whose children are ignored by accessibility (.accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)), so it is never in the tree, and the vocabulary has no hover step (window.capacity's case). The same toggle is the row's "Show details" accessibility action and Space on the grid, and db-detail-strip.jsonl drives Space (open, close, another row). Pressing the ⓘ itself is walk-only.

a Text (3b-v, Rule 8): settings.json's read or parse error, drawn only when ~/.wakil/settings.json cannot be read. The seed never writes that file, and no step can write it mid-launch — editor writes are confined to the active project's roots (Invariant 6, Decision 36) and ~/.wakil is outside them; display text with no press action either way. Its wording and the defaults it leaves in force are pinned by internal/wakilcore/editorsettings_test.go and WakilKitTests EditorSettingsTests; the runbook walks it with a hand-broken file.

a Text (3b-v, Rule 8): drawn only when Go refuses a word-wrap write the pane itself offers (On or Off), and Go refuses a boolean only when settings.json does not parse — which, as for settings.editor.error, no fixture or step can produce. Display text with no press action. 3b-v-editor-settings-nodes.jsonl drives both choices and asserts each write on disk.

a Text (3b-v, Rule 8): drawn only when Go refuses an autosave mode the pane offers (off, pause, focus are each valid), which happens only over a settings.json that does not parse — no fixture or step can produce one (settings.editor.error's reason). Display text with no press action. 3b-v-editor-settings-nodes.jsonl drives all three modes and asserts each on disk.

a Text (3b-v, Rule 8): drawn only when Go refuses Spaces or Tabs, which it does only for a project.json filed under another organisation or unreadable — and either one drops the project from the settings tree, so its Editor node draws `gone` instead of this form and the refusal has nowhere to appear. Display text with no press action. 3b-v-project-editor-settings.jsonl drives both choices (Tabs through parity) and asserts each on disk.

the editor's left column's container (.contain, 3b-ii): its header, the tree or the search view, and the edge, and it takes no input itself. What it draws is read by every 3b-ii-* check; its controls are editor.column.files / .search, pressed by 3b-ii-tree-toggle.jsonl, editor.column.edge, dragged there, and the tree's and search's own.

the tree's load tick (3b-ii, Rule 5): a shape drawn only while a root lists or a heavy folder loads, which against the fixture's small roots lasts milliseconds — never long enough for a tree read to see (git.loading's case). 3b-ii-tree-ignored-heavy.jsonl asserts what the load brings (autoload.php under vendor); seeing the tick is the runbook's walk.

a Text (3b-ii, Rule 8): a root's or a heavy folder's listing error, drawn whole under its row. Every fixture root lists and vendor loads, and no step can make one unreadable mid-launch; display text with no press action either way. Pinned by WakilKitTests (EditorTreeTests), and an unreadable root is the runbook's walk.

a Text (3b-ii): "only the first 50,000 files are listed", drawn only under a root whose listing hit the cap. The fixture's roots hold a few hundred files and seeding 50,000 per launch is not worth its minute; a note row is never selected or pressed. Its row is pinned by WakilKitTests (EditorTreeTests).
a Text (3b-ii, Rule 8): a search's error, drawn whole. Read, not pressed — 3b-ii-search-errors.jsonl asserts "missing closing )" in the tree and through read_pane, with the typed query kept.

a Text (3b-ii): "only the first 2,000 matches are shown", drawn only over a search that hit the cap. 2,000 matches are not seeded; `truncated` is pinned by internal/wakilcore/files_test.go and WakilKitTests (EditorSearchActionsTests), and the note is the runbook's walk.

a Text (3b-ii): "only the first 50,000 files are searched", drawn only when a root's listing hit the cap. 50,000 files are not seeded (editor.tree.note:<…>'s reason); `files_truncated` is pinned by internal/wakilcore/files_test.go and WakilKitTests (EditorSearchActionsTests).

the search tick (3b-ii, Rule 5): a shape with no press action, drawn while a search is in flight. Read, not pressed — 3b-ii-search-cancel.jsonl reads the tree for its label, "searching", with no read_pane or other dispatch ending while the search runs (the regex switch is set on the empty query first, so typing starts the one search), so only the window's editor-flight redraw (final review C1) can draw it; it then presses the Cancel beside it, editor.search.cancel.

the Search view's cancelled line's container (.contain, 3b-ii walk): the Text "search cancelled" and its Re-run, editor.search.rerunCancelled. Read, not pressed — 3b-ii-search-cancel.jsonl asserts "search cancelled" in the tree and search.cancelled through read_pane after Cancel, then presses Re-run and reads the search running again with cancelled cleared.

a Text (3b-ii walk): "no matches", drawn under a finished search that found nothing. Display text with no press action. Read, not pressed — 3b-ii-search.jsonl asserts it in the tree after a search for a string no fixture file holds.

the replace's result line's container (.contain, 3b-ii-b): the summary Text, Undo replace (editor.replace.undo, pressed) and the failures under it. Read, not pressed — 3b-ii-b-replace-all.jsonl asserts "Replaced 3 in 3 files" in the tree and last_replace through read_pane; 3b-ii-b-replace-undo.jsonl asserts "Undid the replace in 2 files".

a Text (3b-ii-b, Rule 8): one file the replace or its undo could not write or put back, drawn whole. Read, not pressed — 3b-ii-b-replace-undo.jsonl asserts "changed since the replace — left as it is" in the tree for the file changed on disk after the replace.

the replace tick (3b-ii-b, Rule 5): a shape with no press action, drawn while a replace or its undo is in flight (editor.search.busy's case). Read, not pressed — 3b-ii-b-replace-cancel.jsonl reads the tree for its label, "replacing", while the replace walks the 200 MiB haystack, then presses the Cancel beside it, editor.replace.cancel.

not a control (3b-ii-b): the name of a SwiftUI coordinate space (`.coordinateSpace(name: "editor.tabs")`, the tab strip's, which the drop target and the middle-click measure in), not an accessibility identifier.
